Dear Editor,

Please consider our manuscript, *Insurance coverage, service use, and payment at outpatient contact among adults with disability in Kenya before the SHA transition: a secondary analysis of KDHS 2022*, for publication as a Research Article.

Using the KDHS 2022 person recode, we measure disability with the Washington Group Short Set and estimate insurance coverage, outpatient service use, and payment at the last outpatient contact among 40,197 adults. Adults meeting the disability threshold had lower insurance coverage than adults without disability (24.5% versus 31.6%), coverage fell with severity of functional difficulty (to 19.7% at severe difficulty), and outpatient use was nearly twice as high (42.0% versus 22.0%). Payment at the last outpatient visit remained near-universal in both groups, and within the disability subpopulation holding insurance was not associated with lower odds of paying (APR 0.98, 95% CI 0.92 to 1.04).

The paper matters now because Kenya's Social Health Insurance Act 2023 created an exemption pathway for some persons with severe disability, and KDHS 2022 is the last nationally representative measurement before the Social Health Authority transition on 1 October 2024. It therefore establishes the baseline against which that exemption must be judged, using the Washington Group Short Set carried in that round to disaggregate coverage, service use, and payment by functional difficulty.

The manuscript is original, is not under consideration elsewhere, and uses authorised de-identified survey microdata. All authors have approved the submission and declare no competing interests.

Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,
